newsitem.title: UK: ACPC draft proposal to keep quotas, add flexibility.
newsitem.headline: ACPC draft proposal to keep quotas, add flexibility.

text.p: A draft proposal for a full session of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) that is to meet on Wednesday would have the group retain export quotas but include new flexibility on allocating them, delegates said.
The delegates were speaking after a preparatory session of the ACPC 6-member technical group. The ACPC is considering a response to volatile prices in the world market.

Earlier, Monday's six-member technical meeting ended with an agreement on a proposal to submit to a full session on Wednesday, ACPC chairman Rubens Barbosa of Brazil said. But he declined to specify what proposal was.
"There is an agreement on a proposal to be submitted to the council at their meeting on Wednesday," Barbosa said.
A delegation source later said "Nothing is going to change. We are going to keep the same system" But the ACPC would be looking at "flexibility in the allocation in the quotas".
The delegate said the market needed specific types of coffee.
"There are robustas, washed, mild and so on...so we are starting on how to discuss the flexibility of what the market is wanting right now...that is the main idea".
